findings.title: Cache key uses process-randomized hash()
findings.body: The cache key is built as `f"error_upsampling_eligible:{organization.id}:{hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))}"`. In CPython 3.3+, the hash of tuples and strings is randomized per process (PYTHONHASHSEED). Different web/worker processes will therefore generate different cache keys for the same organization/project set, so the cache will only ever hit within a single process. This defeats the stated 60-second cross-request caching optimization and causes every request in a multi-worker deployment to miss the cache and re-read the allowlist option. Replace `hash(...)` with a deterministic digest (e.g. `hashlib.md5(str(sorted_ids).encode()).hexdigest()`) or just inline the sorted ids into the key.

findings.title: Duplicate alias when query has multiple count() columns
findings.body: `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` always replaces `count()` with the literal string `"upsampled_count() as count"`. If `query_columns` ever contains more than one `count()` entry (e.g. `["count()", "count()"]` or `["count()", "count_unique(user)", "count()"]`), the resulting SQL has two columns aliased `count`, which ClickHouse/Snuba will reject and the endpoint will return 500. The function should uniquify the alias (e.g. `upsampled_count() as count`, `upsampled_count() as count_2`, ...) or track a counter.

findings.title: Sample rate not range-validated and applied to all event types
findings.body: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` blindly does `float(client_sample_rate)` and assigns it to `normalized_data["sample_rate"]` whenever the value is truthy. There is no check that the value lies in (0, 1]; out-of-range, NaN, or negative values from a malformed SDK payload will be accepted and propagated into the event's `sample_rate`, which downstream logic (including the new `upsampled_count() = sum(sample_weight)` aggregation) relies on. A negative or >1 rate will produce nonsensical or negative upsampled counts. Additionally, the helper is called from `store_event` for every event, not just errors, so a transaction that coincidentally carries an `error_sampling` context will also get `sample_rate` set. The validation should reject values outside (0, 1] and the call site should be gated on event type or at least the presence of the context.

findings.title: Substring match for event.type:error produces false positives
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` does `if "event.type:error" in query` on the lowercased raw query string. This matches `NOT event.type:error` (the user is explicitly excluding errors) and `event.type:error_handled`, both of which are not error-focused queries. In those cases `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` will return True for the discover dataset, `count()` will be rewritten to `sum(sample_weight)`, and the returned counts will be wrong (or, for the NOT case, non-zero when the user asked for non-errors). The check should at minimum look for the token as a standalone segment (e.g. whitespace-delimited) or use the existing search-query tokenizer.

findings.title: Cache invalidation helper is defined but never called
findings.body: `invalidate_upsampling_cache(organization_id, project_ids)` is exported and its docstring says "This should be called when the allowlist configuration changes to ensure cache consistency across the system." However, nothing in this PR (or anywhere visible in the diff) calls it - the allowlist is read via `options.get("issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist", [])` and there is no signal/listener that fires when that option changes. In practice the 60s TTL will mask allowlist edits, but the helper is dead code and its existence is misleading; either wire it up at the option-set site or remove it.

findings.title: Public is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects is untested
findings.body: The test file only covers the private helpers (`_are_all_projects_error_upsampled`, `_is_error_focused_query`, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`, `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling`). The public entry point `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`, which is what the endpoint actually calls and which contains the cache read/write logic, the AND-composition of allowlist eligibility with the per-call dataset/query check, and the cache-key construction (including the process-randomized `hash()` bug), is not exercised at all. Likewise `invalidate_upsampling_cache` has no test. The endpoint-level tests in `test_organization_events_stats.py` only verify the numeric output of one path and would not catch regressions in the cache logic, the substring-match false positives, or the duplicate-alias case.

findings.title: Missing tests for duplicate count() and other aggregation functions
findings.body: `test_transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` only checks the single-`count()` case. It does not cover (a) multiple `count()` entries in the same input list (which triggers the duplicate-`as count` alias bug), (b) other aggregations that the function intentionally leaves alone such as `count_unique(user)`, `count_if(...)`, or equation columns like `equation|count()`, or (c) the case-insensitive / whitespace behavior of those non-`count()` columns. Adding these cases would have caught the duplicate-alias bug.
